# Tabs

A tab strip with its panels. Tabs go into the tablist and every other child, usually Panels, renders after it.

Also asked as: switch views, tab bar, segmented, view switcher.

**Import:** `import { Tabs } from '@/components';`

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/navigation/Tabs/Tabs.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/navigation/Tabs/Tabs.stories.jsx` — Overview, Layout, Alignment, Appearance, WithPanels, InteractionStates, Interactive, Rest, Hovered, Pressed, Focused, Selected, SelectedPill, Disabled

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/navigation/Tabs/Tabs.mdx`

## Usage

Use `Tabs` for the tab bar that switches between sibling views of the same
subject — a student's Overview / Sessions / Progress, or the sections of an
admin page. Compose it from `Tabs.Tab` children, and declare a `Tabs.Panel`
alongside each one when the tab's content should be owned by the component
rather than rendered separately.

It can be uncontrolled (`defaultActiveKey`) or controlled (`activeKey` plus
`onSelect`). `alignment` covers left, center, right and `justified`, which
stretches the tabs to fill the bar. `appearance` is `default` (an underline) or
`pill` (a filled, rounded selected tab); `spacing` is `default` (32px) or
`compact` (24px).

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Use nouns that name the view: “Sessions”. | Use verbs or full sentences. |
| Write labels in sentence case, one to two words. | Use Title Case or labels that wrap. |
| Keep the same labels across visits. | Rename a tab to show a count or status. |
| Order tabs by how often people open them, most used first. | Hide the most used view in the last tab. |

## Best practices

### A controlled bar needs `onSelect`, or it will never move. {#a-controlled-bar-needs-onselect-or-it-will-never-move}

```jsx
// Incorrect — activeKey pins the bar and nothing updates it.
<Tabs activeKey="overview">
  <Tabs.Tab eventKey="overview">Overview</Tabs.Tab>
  <Tabs.Tab eventKey="sessions">Sessions</Tabs.Tab>
</Tabs>

// Correct.
<Tabs activeKey={tab} onSelect={setTab}>
  <Tabs.Tab eventKey="overview">Overview</Tabs.Tab>
  <Tabs.Tab eventKey="sessions">Sessions</Tabs.Tab>
</Tabs>
```

### Every `Tabs.Tab` needs an `eventKey` — selection is keyed off it. {#every-tabs-tab-needs-an-eventkey-selection-is-keyed-off-it}

```jsx
// Incorrect — with no eventKey, there is no key to compare against activeKey,
// so the tab never shows as selected and onSelect fires with nothing useful.
<Tabs activeKey={tab} onSelect={setTab}>
  <Tabs.Tab>Overview</Tabs.Tab>
</Tabs>

// Correct.
<Tabs activeKey={tab} onSelect={setTab}>
  <Tabs.Tab eventKey="overview">Overview</Tabs.Tab>
</Tabs>
```

### Keep the labels short and parallel. {#keep-the-labels-short-and-parallel}

Each label is one or two words naming a view of the same subject: Overview, Sessions, Progress. Parallel wording lets people scan the strip without reading it.

Do: Short nouns for views of the same subject.
Don't: Mixed verbs and phrases that do not scan.

### Choose the appearance by weight, not taste. {#choose-the-appearance-by-weight-not-taste}

The underline suits a strip that sits above page content. The pill suits a strip inside a card or toolbar, where a filled selected tab reads as a control.

Do: A pill strip inside a card reads as a control.
Don't: The page-level underline inside a card, where it reads as a stray rule.

### Keep labels the same across visits. {#keep-labels-the-same-across-visits}

A label names a view. A count or status in it changes the name and breaks the parallel wording.

Do: The label names the view.
Don't: Counts and status in the label.

## Accessibility

- **A real tab widget, always.** `role="tablist"` on the strip, `role="tab"`
  and `aria-selected` on each tab, `aria-controls` pointing at the panel when
  one is declared, and roving tabindex: one stop for the whole strip, with
  Left, Right, Home and End moving selection and focus together. Tabs are real
  `<button>` elements, so activating one pushes no history entry and moves no
  scroll position.
- **A disabled tab stays reachable by the arrow keys**, so its existence is
  discoverable, but is never selected — `isDisabled` keeps it out of
  `activeKey` contention without removing it from the strip's keyboard path.
- **`aria-controls` is omitted rather than dangled.** A `Tabs.Tab` with no
  matching `Tabs.Panel` gets no pointer at all — an id that is not in the
  document sends assistive technology to nothing, which is worse than pointing
  nowhere.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `children` | node | — | `Tabs.Tab` elements, which fill the tablist, and the `Tabs.Panel` elements that follow it. |
| `alignment` | enum | `'left'` | Horizontal alignment of the tab strip |
| `appearance` | enum | `'default'` | Underline indicator (default), or a pill-shaped selected fill. |
| `spacing` | enum | `'default'` | `default` is a 32px tab; `compact` is 24px. |
| `className` | string | `''` | Extra class on the tabs root, beside `plus-tabs`. |
| `id` | string | — | Id set on the tabs root. |
| `defaultActiveKey` | string or number | — | The `eventKey` of the tab selected at first, for uncontrolled use. |
| `activeKey` | string or number | — | The `eventKey` of the selected tab, for controlled use. Pair it with `onSelect`. |
| `onSelect` | func | — | Called with the newly selected `eventKey` whenever selection moves. |

## Variants

**`alignment`** — `left` · `center` · `right` · `justified`

**`appearance`** — `default` · `pill`

**`spacing`** — `default` · `compact`

Anything not listed is not a valid value.

## Sub-components

### `Tabs.Tab`

Implemented as `Tab`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `eventKey` | string or number | — | Identifies this tab; matched against the root's `activeKey`/`defaultActiveKey`. |
| `children` | node | — | The tab's label. |
| `isDisabled` | bool | — | Disables this tab: it cannot be selected. |
| `className` | string | — | Extra class on the tab, beside `plus-tab`. |

### `Tabs.Panel`

Implemented as `Panel`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `eventKey` | string or number | — | Matches the `Tab` with the same `eventKey`. |
| `children` | node | — | The content shown while the matching tab is selected. |
| `className` | string | — | Extra class on the panel, beside `plus-tabs-panel`. |

## Related

- For navigating to a different page, use the Top bar pattern or `Breadcrumb` — tabs imply the content stays in place.
- For more tabs than fit the width, use `Select` — the strip is `flex-wrap: wrap`, so the overflow becomes a second row of tabs rather than a scroll or an overflow menu, and the row the reader is on stops being obvious.
- For filtering a list rather than switching between views, use `Select` or `RadioGroup` — filters combine, tabs do not.

Same group: `Breadcrumb` · `Link` · `MenuGroup` · `Pagination` · `Sidebar`
